note.note:
Consult Summary:
- 58-year-old female with 5 days of dry cough and persistent rhinorrhea, suspected viral chest infection; diabetic and hypertensive; advised symptomatic care, temperature monitoring, and to recontact if fever persists/worsens or respiratory symptoms deteriorate.

History:
- Presenting complaint:
  - 5 days of cough and constant streaming/runny nose.
  - Cough described as frequent, dry, occurring every ~20–30 minutes.
  - Nasal discharge described as green.
- Timeline/progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately five days ago.
  - Some symptomatic improvement with oral Lemsip (soothes throat, especially at night).
  - Initial brief episode of diarrhea around onset; resolved.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Lemsip (lemon) taken 2–3 times daily, provides throat relief and helps sleep.
  - No other self-treatment documented.
- Associated symptoms / review of systems:
  - Subjective feeling of being hot at times and chills at other times; no home thermometer check performed.
  - Myalgias/achiness.
  - No sputum production from cough.
  - No hemoptysis.
  - No chest pain.
  - No shortness of breath or pleuritic pain.
  - Eating and drinking normal; passing urine normal.
  - No current vomiting or diarrhea.
  - No rash, no headache, no vision changes.
  - No sore ears reported.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Denies fever measured with thermometer (not checked).
  - Denies ongoing diarrhea, vomiting.
  - Denies recurrent chest infections or chronic chest problems.
  - Denies known medication allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
  - Recent blood test approximately 3 weeks ago reported as "normal" (specific test and value not documented).
- Hypertension.
- Medications:
  - Metformin — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Lisinopril — dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Patient stated "two hundred" when asked about lisinopril dose; dose/route/frequency not documented; conflict noted.
- Allergies:
  - Seasonal allergic rhinitis / hay fever (patient reports occasional hay fever); no medication allergies reported.

Social History:
- Lives with partner and a dog.
- Occupation: office manager.
- Tobacco use: not documented / patient did not provide an answer when asked.
- Alcohol: reports occasional alcohol intake ("the odd cherry") — frequency/quantity not further specified.
- No other substance use documented.
- Financial or lifestyle factors: none documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: not recorded in transcript.
- Examination findings: none documented.

Investigations:
- No investigations, imaging, or point-of-care tests performed during consult.
- Patient reports a blood test approximately 3 weeks ago that was "normal" (specific test not documented).

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute upper respiratory infection / likely viral chest infection
  - Assessment:
    - 5-day history of dry cough and green nasal discharge; systemic symptoms of subjective fever/chills and myalgia; no signs of respiratory compromise documented.
    - Likely viral etiology but diabetic status increases risk of secondary bacterial infection.
  - Plan:
    - Symptomatic care advised: continue Lemsip (contains paracetamol) for symptomatic relief.
    - Avoid additional paracetamol-containing products while using Lemsip.
    - Cough suppressants discouraged during daytime; short-term use at night acceptable if cough prevents sleep.
    - Obtain an accurate oral temperature with a thermometer; monitor for persistent fevers.
    - Reassess / seek medical attention if any of the following occur:
      - Persistent temperature >37.5–38°C or recurrent spiking fevers.
      - Worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, hemoptysis, new or worsening shortness of breath, or chest pain.
    - If not improving or if concerning features develop, consider evaluation for bacterial infection and possible antibiotic therapy.
- Issue 2: Diabetes mellitus — monitoring
  - Assessment:
    - Diabetes noted; recent blood test ~3 weeks ago reported normal (unspecified).
  - Plan:
    - Ensure routine diabetes follow-up and monitoring per GP instructions.
    - Patient advised to monitor blood glucose if she has home equipment (patient reported not having blood sugar checking equipment at time of consult).
- Issue 3: Hypertension — monitoring
  - Assessment:
    - Hypertension on treatment with lisinopril; last BP check unspecified.
  - Plan:
    - Continue antihypertensive as prescribed.
    - Advise regular blood pressure checks with GP as arranged.
    - Clarify medication doses with patient’s records or GP (lisinopril dose unclear).
- General plan items:
  - No immediate investigations ordered during consult.
  - Safety netting: return for review or urgent care if symptoms worsen as outlined above.
  - Patient education provided regarding typical viral course (may take 1–2 weeks) and when antibiotics may be required.
